reasonToGo: Everything moving between sea and river changes hulls here, and whatever goes over the side in the change stays on the flats.

hazards.name: The turning tide
hazards.description: The sea pushes up as far as the landing twice a day and pulls back out. A boat left on the wrong side of it sits until evening.
hazards.note: Absence hazard: a tide moves the ground, it does not apply an effect to a body. No runtime zoneHazards type fits.

hazards.name: The low-water mud
hazards.description: Grey mud a foot deep where the boats sit at low water. It takes a boot first and then the leg, and holds a man where he stands.

resources.name: Old plank
resources.description: Hull boards, cleats and sound timber pulled off the barges in the hull change and sewn into new building.

resources.name: Cut reed
resources.description: Reed cut off the brackish fringe at low water, bundled for thatch and for winter bedding.

landmarks.name: The barge-cranes
landmarks.description: Timber jibs standing over the pilings, one to each berth, with the hull-change gear stacked beneath them.

landmarks.name: The rook flats
landmarks.description: Open mud south of the landing, black with rooks working it at every low water.
